title: Turnip: modeled ₹198/qtl left, Kangra (Baijnath) → Shimla
summary: February 2021: reported turnip prices at Kangra (Baijnath) and Shimla imply a positive modeled margin after costs on 78% of 18 matched days; a morning-report back-test averages ₹198 per quintal. No actual trade verified.
why_selected: Selected from 20 same-variety market pairs screened for turnip in February 2021; best tested candidate among the bounded set of routed finalists, not a global optimum.

evidence.observations: daily modal prices for the same variety and grade (FAQ) at both markets; sale matched to the first Shimla report 1–3 days after purchase
caveats: Back-test on reported prices: no actual shipment, buyer or seller is claimed.
Modal prices are reported daily aggregates, not offers anyone could be sure to get.
This data has no arrival volumes, so it cannot show whether the destination could absorb more supply; no capital-constrained or volume allocation optimum is claimed.

Costs extrapolate onion survey values (including to other crops) plus stated allowances, not freight quotes; OSRM car routing, not a verified truck route. Representative town points may not be at mandi gates.
Historical: this says what paid then, not what pays today.

scenes.headline: February 2021
scenes.caption: Kangra (Baijnath) (Himachal Pradesh) and Shimla (Himachal Pradesh) both reported turnip prices for the same variety and grade (FAQ) on 18 matched days.

scenes.headline: Two markets, two prices
scenes.caption: Kangra (Baijnath) reported a median ₹900 per quintal. Shimla reported a median ₹1,125 around modeled arrival days. These are not offers.

scenes.headline: Gap ₹325/qtl
scenes.caption: The median gap was ₹325 per quintal, and Shimla was dearer on 78% of days.

scenes.headline: 214 km by road
scenes.caption: 214 km on OpenStreetMap roads (~4 hours by car). A loaded truck is slower, so we allow 1 days plus 7 days to get paid.

scenes.headline: After modeled costs
scenes.caption: Freight ≈₹46/qtl, 5% fees and commission, loading, 5% loss and interest. On the typical day ₹132 per quintal was left.

scenes.headline: Still positive under stress
scenes.caption: With 25% dearer freight, 10% loss and costlier credit, the typical day still kept ₹58 per quintal.

scenes.headline: A trader who only knew the morning's news
scenes.caption: Using only the latest available Shimla report, the rule selects 14 of 18 modeled shipping days. 12 had positive modeled net, averaging ₹198 per quintal (₹128 under stress).

scenes.headline: The back-test
scenes.caption: The modeled Turnip route from Kangra (Baijnath) to Shimla was positive on 78% of matched days in February 2021. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹19,800, or ₹12,800 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.

assumptions.value: onion survey freight applied per quintal to turnip
scaled by road km against the 1,115 km Lasalgaon→Azadpur route → ₹46/qtl here
12% a year (14% adverse) for transit + 7 days
~450 road km a day → 1 days here

conclusion: The modeled Turnip route from Kangra (Baijnath) to Shimla was positive on 78% of matched days in February 2021. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹19,800, or ₹12,800 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.

sources.title: Agmarknet / data.gov.in daily mandi modal prices (retained AGRINET snapshot)
RBI Working Paper WPS (DEPR) 08/2024 — Price Dynamics of Tomato, Onion and Potato
